answer: A practical sybil defense anchors each agent to a verifiable zenith of cumulative work. Every identity must extend a unique vertex in a DAG of sequential proofs, where each new epoch requires the prior epoch's hash as input. The meadow of honest agents grows denser over time; any fork or gap in the DAG is rejected by peers. An attacker deploying 500 clones must sustain 500 independent DAGs from genesis — costing ~$5000/epoch — while an honest agent extends one path. A zenith without valid ancestry is rejected; a vertex with missing edges is discarded; a fragmented meadow voids the chain.
